messages.content:
Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The ants collide as follows:

1. **A and B** start 30 cm apart, closing at \(3+1=4\) cm/s, so they meet after  
   \(30/4 = 15/2\) s at \(x = 10 + 3(15/2) = 65/2\) cm.  
   After bouncing: A moves left at 3 cm/s, B moves right at 1 cm/s.  
   C is still moving left at 2 cm/s and is at \(80 - 2(15/2) = 65\) cm.

2. From \(t=15/2\):
   - A heads left from \(65/2\) cm to 0 at 3 cm/s, taking \((65/2)/3 = 65/6\) s.  
     So A falls at \(t = 15/2 + 65/6 = 55/3\) s.
   - B (at \(65/2\), moving right at 1) and C (at 65, moving left at 2) approach each other with closing speed 3 cm/s and gap \(65 - 65/2 = 65/2\) cm. They meet after \((65/2)/3 = 65/6\) s, i.e. also at \(t = 55/3\) s, at  
     \(x = 65/2 + 65/6 = 130/3\) cm.  
     At this instant A falls off the left end, and B and C bounce: B reverses to move left at 1 cm/s, C reverses to move right at 2 cm/s.

3. After \(t = 55/3\):
   - C moves right from \(130/3\) cm to 100 cm: distance \(100 - 130/3 = 170/3\) cm at 2 cm/s, taking \(85/3\) s.  
     C falls at \(t = 55/3 + 85/3 = 140/3\) s.
   - B moves left from \(130/3\) cm to 0 cm: distance \(130/3\) cm at 1 cm/s, taking \(130/3\) s.  
     B falls at \(t = 55/3 + 130/3 = 185/3\) s.

The last ant (B) falls off at \(185/3\) seconds.

ANSWER: 185/3
